newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST -Australian Sports News - Oct 25.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST -Australian Sports News - Oct 25.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Saintly is seen as the horse to come between joint favourites Juggler and Filante and victory in tomorrow's A$1.5 million Cox Plate. Saintly ran well yesterday morning at Flemington as he rounded off his build-up for the weight-for-age event. Page 22.

Australian baseball pitcher Graeme Lloyd of the New York Yankees is the talk of the town after his great pitching effort pulled the Yankees back from defeat against the Atlanta Braves in the longest games in world series history yesterday. Page 21.

Former Balmain rugby league great Keith Barnes is in Royal North Shore's intensive care unit after suffering problems encountered during knee surgery earlier this week. Barnes is in a serious but stable state and is gradually improving, according to Balmin chief executive Danny Munk. Page 20.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

In his 100th rugby union Test match, David Campese was nervous leading the Australian Wallabies onto the field, as the last time he led the team out in 1990 they lost. While Campese has more often than not run out last as a good luck charm, the Australia team still defeated Italy 40-18. Page 40.

Former Australian tennis representative Wally Masur is taking the opportunity of helping player Michael Stich lift his slipping tennis game. Both will use the team up of coach and player as a test, after Masur turned down an offer to coach Goran Ivanisevc earlier this year. Page 39.

Midway through the nine-day Commonwealth Bank Cycling Classic, two New Zealanders and an Australian tussled for line honours in the leg around Sydney's Centennial Park. However, the cyclists' starring efforts made little impression on the overall standins, which see Sven Teutenberg as leader. Page 39.
THE AGE

The Victoria Racing Club yesterday dismissed its current blood sampling tests as unworkable and has recommended sweeping changes to the rules after the Encosta de Lago affair. One recommendation is the slashing of the legal limit of bicarbonate in horses Page C12.

If the City of Maribyrnong backs down on its agreement to clear the Footscray club of its A$1.8 million debt, the club will not be able to change its name to the proposed Western Bulldogs and shift to Optus Oval in a new revitalisation of the club's outlook. Page C12.

Australian cricketer Adam Gilchrist may not be able to distinguish a dream from a nightmare as he makes his cricket debut for Australia in India. Facing a tough South African outfit, Gilchrist will be suffering future shock, culture shock, and jet lag. Page C9.
HERALD SUN

Victoria Racing Club chief executive Brain Beattie yesterday confirmed that his club would table its thoughts on the issue of pre-race blood testing. The club will today officially recommend the legal level of bicarbonate in horses be dropped from 37 to 5 millimoles. Page. 108.

Sydney Swans AFL lead kicker Tony Lockett has gone under the knife to fix up a list of injuries aggravated by last season. Lockett has had a hernia repaired, a degenerated kneecap fixed, and work done on his cartilage. Page 106.

Bruce Bolden the former captain and championship forward of the Melbourne Magics basketball team has said the Magic has no chance to stop Andrew Gaze unless Darren Lucas is given the job to stop him. Page 101.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Horse trainer Gai Waterhouse has rated Juggler the best horse she has ever trained and says it compares well with former Horse of the Year and 1984 Cox Plate winner Red Anchor. Tomorrow is the running of the A$1.5 million BMW Cox Plate (2040m) at Moonee Valley. Page 112.

Australian golfer Robert Allenby, suffering injuries from a recent car accident, was forced to compete in Valderrama yesterday to qualify for his European tour bonus. His one shot before retiring did not even make it past the ladies' tee, yet it earned hm a A$150,000 bonus which he will donate to two cancer charities. Page 110.

Cereal giant Uncle Tobys will at the end of the season split with ironmen race organisers International Management Group and Iron Man Super Series. The move confirms reports of shaky relations between the parties. Page 104.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
